arxiv-2105-08056.title: A graphene edge-mediated quantum gate
arxiv-2105-08056.creator: Phillip Weinberg, Adrian E. Feiguin
arxiv-2105-08056.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Phillip Weinberg, Adrian E. Feiguin. We propose a quantum gate architecture that allows for the systematic control of the effective exchange interactions between magnetic impurities embedded in nano-scale graphene flakes connected by a gated bridge. The entanglement between the magnetic moment and the edge states of the fragments is used to electrostatically tune the exchange interaction from ferro to antiferromagnetic by merely changing the bridge’s carrier density.

arxiv-2108-09366.title: Multi-boundary generalization of thermofield double states and their realization in critical quantum spin chains
arxiv-2108-09366.creator: Yijian Zou, Guifre Vidal
arxiv-2108-09366.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yijian Zou, Guifre Vidal. We propose a multi-boundary generalization of thermofield double states (TFD) of a two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT) and show, through a conformal map to the complex plane, that they are closely related to multi-point correlation functions. We then also describe how to approximately realize these multi-boundary TFD states numerically on the lattice, starting from a critical quantum spin chain Hamiltonian.

arxiv-2207-05263.title: Ram pressure stripping of the multiphase ISM: a detailed view from TIGRESS simulations Athena ( Stone et al. 2008 ; Stone & Gardiner 2009 ) , astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , scipy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 ) , numpy ( van der Walt et al. 2011 ) , IPyt
arxiv-2207-05263.creator: Woorak Choi, Chang-Goo Kim, Aeree Chung
arxiv-2207-05263.description: Abstract Ram pressure stripping (RPS) is a process that removes the interstellar medium (ISM) quickly, playing a vital role in galaxy evolution. Previous RPS studies have treated the ISM as single-phase or lack the resolution and physical processes to properly capture the full multiphase ISM.

arxiv-2310-00636.title: A DEIM-CUR factorization with iterative SVDs Journal: xxxxx
arxiv-2310-00636.creator: Perfect Y. Gidisu, Michiel E. Hochstenbach
arxiv-2310-00636.description: Abstract A CUR factorization is often utilized as a substitute for the singular value decomposition (SVD), especially when a concrete interpretation of the singular vectors is challenging. Moreover, if the original data matrix possesses properties like nonnegativity and sparsity, a CUR decomposition can better preserve them compared to the SVD.

arxiv-2310-07282.title: An Analysis on Large Language Models in Healthcare: A Case Study of BioBERT
arxiv-2310-07282.creator: Shyni Sharaf, V. S. Anoop
arxiv-2310-07282.description: Abstract This paper conducts a comprehensive investigation into applying large language models, particularly on BioBERT, in healthcare. It begins with thoroughly examining previous natural language processing (NLP) approaches in healthcare, shedding light on the limitations and challenges these methods face.

arxiv-2312-08847.title: Knowledge-Driven Modulation of Neural Networks with Attention Mechanism for Next Activity Prediction
arxiv-2312-08847.creator: Ivan Donadello ∗, Jonghyeon Ko ∗, Fabrizio Maria Maggi ∗, Jan Mendling †, Francesco Riva ‡, Matthias Weidlich †
arxiv-2312-08847.description: Abstract Predictive Process Monitoring (PPM) aims at leveraging historic process execution data to predict how ongoing executions will continue up to their completion. In recent years, PPM techniques for the prediction of the next activities have matured significantly, mainly thanks to the use of Neural Networks (NNs) as a predictor.

arxiv-2312-13861.title: Graph partition method based on finite projective planes
arxiv-2312-13861.creator: Oleg Kruglov, Anna Mastikhina, Oleg Senkevich, Dmitry Sirotkin, Stanislav Moiseev*
arxiv-2312-13861.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Oleg Kruglov, Anna Mastikhina, Oleg Senkevich, Dmitry Sirotkin, Stanislav Moiseev*. We present a novel graph partition algorithm with a theoretical bound for the replication factor of n \sqrt{n} , which improves known constrained approaches (grid: 2 n \sqrt{n} -1, torus: 1.5 n \sqrt{n} +1) and provides better performance.

arxiv-2403-10861.title: FedQNN: Federated Learning using Quantum Neural Networks
arxiv-2403-10861.creator: Nouhaila Innan 1 , Muhammad Al-Zafar Khan 2 , Alberto Marchisio 3,4 , Muhammad Shafique 3,4 , and Mohamed Bennai 1
arxiv-2403-10861.description: Abstract In this study, we explore the innovative domain of Quantum Federated Learning (QFL) as a framework for training Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models via distributed networks. Conventional machine learning models frequently grapple with issues about data privacy and the exposure of sensitive information.

arxiv-2502-15743.title: How Prime Factors Form Fractals
arxiv-2502-15743.creator: Micah D. Tillman (mdtillman@stanford.edu)
arxiv-2502-15743.description: Abstract We explore a new sieve that generates both primes and prime factorizations, without resorting to division. We demonstrate that the integer sequences generated by the sieve are the p p -adic valuations of n n , and that each is a fractal sequence. We then show that these sequences produce geometrical fractals like the Lévy Dragon.

arxiv-2505-22218.title: Aspects of density approximation by tensor trains Thanks: This work was supported by the Czech Science Foundation, project no. P103/22-11101S, and by the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports of the Czech Republic under project ROBOPROX – Robotics and Advanced Industrial Production CZ.02.01.01/00/
arxiv-2505-22218.creator: Jiří Ajgl, Ondřej Straka
arxiv-2505-22218.description: Abstract Point-mass filters solve Bayesian recursive relations by approximating probability density functions of a system state over grids of discrete points. The approach suffers from the curse of dimensionality. The exponential increase of the number of the grid points can be mitigated by application of low-rank approximations of multidimensional arrays.

arxiv-2508-20316.title: Score-Based Diffusion Models in Infinite Dimensions: A Malliavin Calculus Perspective
arxiv-2508-20316.creator: Ehsan Mirafzali, Frank Proske, Daniele Venturi, Razvan Marinescu
arxiv-2508-20316.description: Abstract We develop a new mathematical framework for score-based diffusion modelling in infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert spaces, through Malliavin calculus, extending generative modelling techniques beyond the finite-dimensional setting. The forward diffusion process is formulated as a linear stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) driven by space–time coloured noise with a trace-class covariance operator, ensuring well–posedness in arbitrary spatial dimensions.

europmc-pmc9671806.title: Cemiplimab plus chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone in non-small cell lung cancer: a randomized, controlled, double-blind phase 3 trial.
europmc-pmc9671806.creator: Gogishvili M, Melkadze T, Makharadze T, Giorgadze D, Dvorkin M, Penkov K, Laktionov K, Nemsadze G, Nechaeva M, Rozhkova I, Kalinka E, Gessner C, Moreno-Jaime B, Passalacqua R, Li S, McGuire K, Kaul M, Paccaly A, Quek RGW, Gao B, Seebach F, Weinreich DM, Yancopoulos GD, Lowy I, Gullo G, Rietschel P.
europmc-pmc9671806.description: First-line cemiplimab (anti-programmed cell death-1 (PD-1)) monotherapy has previously shown significant improvement in overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) versus chemotherapy in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (aNSCLC) and PD-ligand 1...

plos-pone-0349292.title: Comparison between enzyme-linked immunospot assay and intracellular cytokine flow cytometry assay of cytomegalovirus-specific T-cell response in healthy participants
plos-pone-0349292.creator: Chompunuch Klinmalai, Nopporn Apiwattanakul, Somsak Prasongtanakij, Jackrapong Bruminhent, Supanart Srisala
plos-pone-0349292.description: Comparison between enzyme-linked immunospot assay and intracellular cytokine flow cytometry assay of cytomegalovirus-specific T-cell response in healthy participants

pmc-10672514.title: A Systematic Review of Curtisia dentata Endemic to South Africa: Phytochemistry, Pharmacology, and Toxicology
pmc-10672514.creator: Maropeng Vellry Raletsena, Ofentse Jacob Pooe, Nkoana Ishmael Mongalo
pmc-10672514.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The use of traditional medicine in treating a variety of both human and animal infections is ancient and still relevant. This is due to the resistance exhibited by most pathogenic microbial stains to currently-used antibiotics. The current work reports the phytochemistry, ethno-medicinal uses, toxicology, and most important pharmacological activities that validate the use of the plant species in African traditional medicine.

pmc-11436904.title: Deep longitudinal lower respiratory tract microbiome profiling reveals genome-resolved functional and evolutionary dynamics in critical illness
pmc-11436904.creator: Minghui Cheng, Yingjie Xu, Xiao Cui, Xin Wei, Yundi Chang, Jun Xu, Cheng Lei, Lei Xue, Yifan Zheng, Zhang Wang, Lingtong Huang, Min Zheng, Hong Luo, Yuxin Leng, Chao Jiang
pmc-11436904.description: The lower respiratory tract (LRT) microbiome impacts human health, especially among critically ill patients. However, comprehensive characterizations of the LRT microbiome remain challenging due to low microbial mass and host contamination. We develop a chelex100-based low-biomass microbial-enrichment method (CMEM) that enables deep metagenomic profiling of LRT samples to recover near-complete microbial genomes.

pmc-11532752.title: Identification of volatile and flavor metabolites in three varieties of broccoli sprouts
pmc-11532752.creator: Yu Xia, Ming-Yue Li, Syed Abdul Wadood, Han-Jun Hong, Yi Liu, Yu-Xuan Luo, Yi-Yan Wang, Hong-Yan Liu, Ren-You Gan
pmc-11532752.description: Broccoli sprouts are promising functional food sources and their taste and flavor play a pivotal role in the acceptance of consumers. In this study, the flavor profiles of three varieties of broccoli sprouts, namely Bi Lv, You Xiu, and Lv Hua, were comprehensively characterized using HS-SPME-GC/MS analysis.

pmc-11633048.title: Edaravone Protects Trophoblast Cells From Hypoxic Injury in Preeclampsia: Inhibition of the PI3K/AKT Pathway as a Promising Therapeutic Approach
pmc-11633048.creator: Xin Liu, Jun Wan, Ming Wei, Yanan Tong, Zhaomin Yao
pmc-11633048.description: ObjectivePreeclampsia (PE) is a multifaceted medical condition that manifests during pregnancy, characterized by hypertension and damage to multiple organs. In PE, the placenta's impaired functionality leads to continuous hypoxia in placental tissues, which is considered the primary cause of the condition. Inhibition of hypoxia‐induced injury in trophoblast cells presents a potential therapeutic strategy for PE.

pmc-12411140.title: Atypical Biliary Fistula After Revisional Bariatric Surgery: A Case Report
pmc-12411140.creator: Venkata Pavan Kumar Karanam, Aarsh Mukeshbhai Panchal, Suresh Kumar Sepuri, Lakshmi Kumar Chalamarla, Phani Krishna Ravula
pmc-12411140.description: Obesity affects about 39% of the global population, and bariatric surgery is a leading treatment option. As the number of primary bariatric procedures increases, so does the demand for revisional bariatric surgeries (RBSs), which are often more complex and associated with increased risks of complications. This case report details an unusual complication of RBS that surgeons should be aware of.

pmc-12534793.title: ﻿Euroscaptor darwini sp. nov., a new species of mole (Mammalia, Eulipotyphla, Talpidae) from the north-central mountains in Vietnam
pmc-12534793.creator: Son Truong Nguyen, Hai Tuan Bui, Vinh Quang Dau, Phuong Dinh Le, Yen Huong Vu
pmc-12534793.description: ﻿AbstractA new species of fossorial mole (Eulipotyphla, Talpidae, Euroscaptor) is described from Pu Luong Nature Reserve, north-central Vietnam, based on distinct genetic and morphological characteristics. The species inhabits a geographically small and isolated upland patch (900–1100 m a.s.l.), sharply bounded by a nearly vertical escarpment.

pmc-12575758.title: Motor learning mechanisms are not modified by feedback manipulations in a real-world task
pmc-12575758.creator: Federico Nardi, A. Aldo Faisal, Shlomi Haar
pmc-12575758.description: Error-based and reward-based mechanisms of motor learning co-occur in real-world scenarios but are traditionally isolated in laboratory tasks via feedback manipulations. We examined the distinctiveness of these mechanisms by applying lab-based feedback manipulations to a real-world task. Using Embodied Virtual Reality of pool billiards, we introduced visual perturbations while maintaining full proprioception.

pmc-13246886.title: SQLE as a potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for LIHC: a multi-cohort and spatial study
pmc-13246886.creator: Jin Xie, Gao-Chun Xiao, Xin-Yang Qu, Rui-Min Wu, Yu-Long Zou, Hao-Shen Yu, Xue Hu, Xu-Sheng Liu
pmc-13246886.description: Liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC) remains a highly aggressive malignancy, necessitating novel biomarkers for early diagnosis and therapeutic intervention. This study investigates the role of Squalene epoxidase (SQLE), a key enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis, in LIHC. Integrating multi-cohort analyses of nine GEO datasets and TCGA revealed significant upregulation of SQLE in LIHC tissues.
